chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

You should say during the last ten days of the month of Ramadan, every night: 'I seek refuge in the Majesty of Your Noble Face lest the month of Ramadan pass me by, or dawn rise from this night of mine, while You have a sin or a debt against me for which You will punish me.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite during the last ten nights of Ramadan?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this supplication emphasizes the anxiety of the believer regarding unexpiated sins or debts (tabi'ah) that might hinder acceptance of worship during the final nights. It reflects the Shia tradition of intense self-accountability (muhasabah) and the hope for divine mercy as Ramadan concludes, ensuring one enters Shawwal with a clean spiritual slate.
